name: SH-60B Seahawk
role: Ship-based anti-submarine and anti-surface warfare helicopter (LAMPS Mk III)

serviceWindow.statusNotes: The SH-60B went operational in 1984 and the US Navy retired it on 11 May 2015, replacing it with the MH-60R. The wider SH-60 family continues in US and allied service in other versions. In the 2026 scenario this is a legacy airframe, kept as the helicopter that Perry-class frigates carried; the Navy itself now flies the MH-60R.

propulsionSummary: Two General Electric T700-GE-401C turboshaft engines, rated at roughly 1,700 to 1,900 shaft horsepower each depending on the source, drive a single four-blade main rotor.

sensors.name: AN/APS-124 search radar
sensors.role: Surface search under the nose; finds ships and surfaced submarines and relays the picture to the parent ship. No public detection range found, so this is an open estimate matching the engine value.

sensors.name: AN/ALQ-142 ESM
sensors.role: Passive radar warning and emitter bearing. No public range found, so this is an open estimate.

sensors.name: Sonobuoys (25-tube launcher) and towed MAD
sensors.role: Air-dropped passive and active sonobuoys listen for submarines and a towed magnetic anomaly detector confirms metal below. Both work only at short range. No public range found, so this is an open estimate.

sensors.name: Optional nose-mounted FLIR turret
sensors.role: Thermal camera for identifying surface contacts. No public range found, so this is an open estimate.

loadouts.name: LAMPS Mk III anti-submarine patrol
loadouts.role: Find and attack submarines ahead of the parent ship using sonobuoys and up to two lightweight torpedoes

loadouts.name: LAMPS Mk III surface patrol
loadouts.role: Radar search and attack against small surface ships with the Hellfire missile, with the Penguin missile as another option and a cabin-door gun for close work

radar.note: A helicopter of this size has a small radar return, but its rotor blades give strong Doppler returns when it hovers.

infrared.note: Two turboshaft engines with exposed exhaust give a clear heat source; an infrared jammer is on some Seahawk versions.

acoustic.note: Rotors make a loud, recognisable noise, and it flies low and slow when it hovers to dip or drop sonobuoys.

visual.note: A 20 m dark helicopter is small but visible at low level in daylight.

brief.whatItIs: The SH-60B Seahawk is the US Navy helicopter built for the LAMPS Mk III system. It lives in the hangar of a frigate, destroyer or cruiser and flies out to find submarines and small ships beyond the ship's own radar horizon. It carries a search radar, sonobuoys, a towed magnetic detector and lightweight torpedoes.
brief.howItIsUsed: A commander launches it to extend the parent ship's eyes by 100 nautical miles or more. In an anti-submarine role it flies a search pattern, drops sonobuoys to listen and then attacks with a torpedo once the target is located. In a surface role it uses radar to see ships, passes the contact to the parent ship and can attack small boats with Hellfire missiles. It is slow, carries little fuel (about 4 hours of mission time) and has no defenses beyond decoys, so keep it away from active fighters and surface-to-air missiles. Its biggest strength is giving a small ship a second set of sensors.
typicalMissions: Anti-submarine search ahead of a ship or convoy
Attack on small surface craft with Hellfire missiles
Search and rescue and vertical replenishment
